how: The program of `fault-LC8008-negative-shift` in real time: `count` takes its default -1 and `core.shl` of an `i32` by a negative count is a fault with no `err` (spec 8.2, A.1 `Bits and integer division`), `LC8008` (spec 8.2, Q-25; cli.md 6.6) at the node `y`, the line `y = core.shl(x, count)`; the mode changes neither the fault nor its place. No loop is around it; no output, no resource, no instrument. In real time `clock` gives `real_ms` only (commands.md 7: `simulated_ms` is for the deterministic mode). Nothing waits before the fault, so the run takes at least 0 ms (the lower bound is a fact); the upper bound, 1000 ms, is a generous tolerance for a machine (README, `runs/`), not derived from the documents.
